### 2026-10-07: October 6th 2026 - Day 1 Research, Feasibility & Component Selection

**3.5h**

October 6th 2026 - Day 1 Research, Feasibility & Component Selection

Things Learnt-

ESP32-S3 main microcontroller with two core Wi-Fi/ BLE processor, SPI & I2C peripherals.

Research on CC1101 Sub-1GHz RF Module to understand how it receives/transmits the RF wave of 315/433/868/915 MHz.

Power Supply was designed. From USB Type-C to TP4056 Battery Charger to 3.3V LDO Voltage Regulator.

Added 6 pin Expansion header to allow for UART/I2C connections in the future to allow for add ons such as GPS, I2S Microphones/Speakers.

No PCB traces were drawn, however I have 80% clarity on what components to use and layout of the schematic.

Key Learnings & Progress:

Researched ESP32-S3 GPIO allocations: learned which pins are safe for general use, which are dedicated for flash/PSRAM, and which pins support native hardware SPI/I2C.

Studied power regulations and voltage requirements for individual modules (ensuring 3.3V tolerance on CC1101 and OLED).

Explored code upload workflows, USB-to-UART bridging versus Native USB flashing on the ESP32-S3, and basic firmware structure for driving the CC1101 transceiver.

No schematic drawing started in this session, but built the technical groundwork required before launching EasyEDA.

EasyEDA Schematic Wiring & Electrical Audit Summary

I have been hard at work for over 2 hours designing my main schematic for AeroDeck-3S. All of my main components have been added (ESP32-S3-WROOM-1, CC1101, MicroSD slot, TP4056, AMS1117, OLED display and 5-way joystick). All connections between the pins on each module have been added. The schematic has been fully audited to ensure no major connection issues.

Progress & Fixes

USB Type-C Connection: The USB Type-C connector was connected using pull down resistors of $5.1\text{ k}\Omega$ on the CC1 and CC2 pins so a regular power delivery can be used. Separating 5V VBUS and 3.3V power rails: Identified 5V VBUS and 3.3V rails were separate to prevent any over-voltage to the ESP32-S3. AMS1117-3.3 pin connections fixed: OUT+ pin from TP4056 was connected to VIN. 3.3V was taken from VOUT. SPI lines corrected on CC1101 and MicroSD slot. SDA and SCL pins changed to IO8 and IO9 respectively on OLED display. The schematic is almost complete and has been fully audited. Time to convert to a 2 layer PCB

### 2026-10-11: Limitations of the ESP32-S3: Initially I had planned to use the popular ESP32-S3, but this did not meet the specifications of the high level power savings, modern processor and latest wireless protoco

**1.18h**

Limitations of the ESP32-S3: Initially I had planned to use the popular ESP32-S3, but this did not meet the specifications of the high level power savings, modern processor and latest wireless protocols needed.

Searching for a better option: I was looking for a chip that would provide better performance, with low power usage and modern connectivity within the $65 budget set by Hack Club.

ESP32-C5-WROOM-1: As a result I chose the ESP32-C5 as my microcontroller. This has a modern RISC-V single core processor, built in Wi-Fi 6 (802.11ax) and Bluetooth 5 connectivity, and is compatible with the sub-1GHz CC1101 module.
